subject: general
question: Which country's constitution has been considered by India for the 'Principles of Liberty, Equality & Fraternity'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**France**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Principles of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity** in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the ideals of the **French Revolution**. 
 
• These principles were deeply influential in the drafting of the **Preamble of the Indian Constitution**, 
 
 
• which emphasizes **justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity** as fundamental values.
 
 
 
• ​The phrase "Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity" originates from the **French Revolution** of 1789 and 
 
 
• represents the core democratic values that influenced many countries, including India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Britain**:

 
 
• India adopted several features from the **British Constitution**, including the **parliamentary system of government**, **rule of law**, **bicameral legislature**, and **single citizenship**. 
 
 
 
• **Australia**:
 
 
• From Australia, India adopted provisions for the **Concurrent List** (subjects shared by the central and state governments) and the **process of a joint sitting of Parliament** to resolve deadlocks. 
 
 
 
• **Ireland**:
 
 
• India adopted the concept of **Directive Principles of State Policy** from Ireland, which was inspired by Ireland’s Constitution.
 
 
 
• These principles guide the Indian state in making policies for social and economic welfare
